Create realistic, production-quality UI design, a full-page desktop web mockup for The Stamp Book, an existing personal national park stamp collection, not a travel booking site.
TARGET: 1440 px wide by 2400 px tall full-page render. One entire coherent scrollable park page only, no collage, no browser/device frame. Keep all content legible. Desktop content capped at 1100px, ample outer whitespace, readable 16px body, comfortable 65-character diary line length, at most two typefaces. Today anchor 2026-09-26; preserve fictional visit dates 19 June 2019 and 21 June 2019.
ATTACHED REFERENCES: existing Yellowstone desktop and collection screens are CONTENT/ASSET references. User REJECTS their clutter and duplication. Do NOT reproduce their three-column layout, repeated stamp imagery, large exposed location sections, dense sidebars or boxes. Third reference is the real Lower Falls photograph to integrate once, faithfully.
CONTENT: Brand The Stamp Book. Park Yellowstone National Park, Wyoming · Montana · Idaho, Rocky Mountain. A subtle 'Sample collection' label. Six distinct blue sample impressions total: two main designs, round Yellowstone geyser and rectangular Yellowstone bison; four smaller substamps: Old Faithful, Grand Prismatic Spring, Grand Canyon of the Yellowstone, Mammoth Hot Springs. Display each of the six artworks ONCE only in this entire page, use horizontal rows/grids, stamps around 90–140px, short readable caption and date. No duplicate sidebar stamp summary. Two visits: 19 June 2019 — Geysers, boardwalks and an evening return (geyser main, Old Faithful, Grand Prismatic); 21 June 2019 — Canyon colours and a northern loop (bison main, canyon, Mammoth). Each visit has a short human note and link to USA road trip 2019.
Diary heading 'Steam, yellow cliffs and the long way round'. Show substantial ORIGINAL fictional prose in 3–4 paragraphs, not lorem ipsum, inspired by this condensed sample: We arrived with a route neatly marked on the map; soon it was mostly a suggestion. Steam beyond the pines and wildlife by the road kept adding stops. Old Faithful was the obvious event, but quieter geyser basins and our evening return stayed with us. At Artist Point, we put the camera away after the photograph and listened to Lower Falls. The northern loop brought Mammoth terraces and wildly changing June weather. Six impressions, two very full days and reasons to return. Label diary fictional subtly; do not pretend this is verified user history.
Use the supplied famous Lower Falls from Artist Point photograph exactly once with small credit NPS / Diane Renkin. Tiny park facts can be a short horizontal line: Established 1872 · Approx. 2.22 million acres, plus Park website / Park maps links. Geographic states already under title must not repeat as a facts table. No map widget required because clutter reduction takes priority; park maps link suffices.
CRITICAL: Stamping locations are rare-use, secondary information. Exactly ONE closed accordion row near bottom, labelled 'Stamping locations · 2' with a right-pointing chevron. No visible location names, descriptions, availability, maps, report history, cards, access instructions, or second location section. It must be visually unmistakably CLOSED.
Navigation minimal: brand, Browse places menu button (collapsed), Search icon/control, maybe Trips. No permanent expanded place tree, no TOC rail, no Appearance rail, no left+right competing sidebars. No badges/metric cards, no enormous action CTA, no gradients, no shadows, no cards-inside-cards. Use typography, spacing, alignment, and only light rules; the full page sits on the page canvas, never in a centered app card. Avoid an empty generic scaffold: all sections filled with realistic content. Show the full composition ending at the footer.

DIRECTION: The Quiet Album. Collection-first contemporary page. Pure white, graphite sans-serif type, modest blue links. Small header, large but restrained left-aligned title, a single quiet facts line. The key composition is one unboxed six-stamp gallery at the top: two main stamps in the first two slots, four substamps in the next four slots, with clear subgroup labels but no duplicates. Below a generous rule, show two lean visit summaries side by side. Then show a medium landscape photograph aligned left with a readable diary text column below. Finish with the single CLOSED locations row. Absolutely no sidebar. Balance generous whitespace with complete content.

DIRECTION: Two Days in Yellowstone. A chronological journal organized into two strong horizontal chapters rather than category sections.
